What I do as a product owner

I was the product owner on every product below. That meant owning each one from the first conversation about the business problem to the release sign-off.

Start from the business problem

Work with the people who live the process to understand what is really going wrong, who it affects and what success looks like, before any solution is drawn.

Write the solution design

Map every business process in BPMN with its actors, events, step catalogue, business rules and screens, precise enough to build from.

Write the PRD

Turn the design into features, user stories and acceptance criteria that developers build against and testers verify.

Guide the build

Keep a features and functionality log, prioritise the backlog with developers, and answer design questions on data, visibility and calculation logic as they come up.

Accept and release

Test what was built against the specification and the PRD, and sign it off only when it behaves as designed.

Lead people and bridge business and technology

Work with cross-functional teams of developers, testers and consultants, and manage subject matter experts and stakeholders, translating between business and technology so requirements are complete, decisions are made on time and everyone agrees on what is being built and why.

Documents I authored for each module: the solution design and the product requirements document (PRD). For Payroll I also kept a features and functionality log that guided developers through the build.

CiBS HCM Suite

CiBS Performance Management

Turning appraisal policy into a fair, auditable cycle

A configuration-driven performance management module covering the full cycle, from cascaded goals to appraisal, moderation, PIPs and succession, with its own workflow, notification and escalation engine.

Suite
CiBS HCM Suite of Applications
Built for
Private and public sector organisations
My role
Product owner
I authored
Solution design and PRD
Platform
Oracle APEX on Oracle Autonomous Database
Scope
16 business processes, 25 roles, 11 analytics reports

The problem

Organisations appraise people in very different ways: self, supervisor and joint ratings, mid-year and year-end reviews, moderation panels, and rules that change by grade. The module had to handle all of it through configuration, for private companies and public-service bodies alike, while keeping every rating auditable.

What I did

  • Wrote the solution design and PRD for the module, covering 16 business processes from goal setting and appraisal to PIPs and succession, with developer-facing template specifications.
  • Defined the calculation logic for a module built from scratch: weighted goal scoring, appraisal-type rating rules, calibration, and the 360-degree feedback design.
  • Answered developers’ questions on data schema and record visibility, so each role sees exactly what policy allows.
Design decisions, process detail and more screenshotsHide the detail

Design decisions that shaped it

Goals cascade from strategy

Every employee goal traces back through intermediate outcomes to a national strategic objective, so alignment is visible on the goal itself.

Approval routing is data, not code

Approval chains are configured per transaction type and department, with reusable conditions such as grade range, position list and org unit deciding when a level applies.

Calibration is a logged step

Pre- and post-calibration ratings are both recorded, and senior leadership endorses the final distribution before it is communicated.

PIPs are a governed case

A performance improvement plan moves through initiation, document preparation, objectives and support, milestone tracking and final reassessment, each with its own approval chain.

CiBS Payroll

Pay that is right, and can prove it

A multi-tenant enterprise payroll product for public and private sector organisations. Every rule is configuration, every committed run is permanent, and every figure can be traced back to the formula that produced it.

Suite
CiBS HCM Suite of Applications
Positioning
Commercial SaaS product for private and public sector organisations across countries
My role
Product owner
I authored
Solution design, PRD and the features and functionality log
Platform
Oracle APEX on Oracle Autonomous Database
Designed for
Up to 100,000 employees per tenant and 50,000 per payroll group

The problem

Payroll errors are legal exposure for the client. The product had to serve very different payrolls (deep public-sector grade and step scales, budget-line costing, variable private-sector pay) from one codebase, with no country’s tax or pension rules hard-coded into the engine.

What I did

  • Wrote the solution design and PRD: twelve end-to-end processes, a calculation engine specification and the product’s own formula language.
  • Built and maintained a features and functionality log for the module that guided developers feature by feature through the build.
  • Shaped the operating model around controls: readiness gates before a run, segregation of duties between configuring, approving and paying, and a period-close checklist that names who owns each open item.
  • Drew on years of Oracle EBS payroll delivery (fast formulas, PAYE and pension reconciliations) to decide what the product must make easy and what it must make impossible.
Design decisions, process detail and more screenshotsHide the detail

Twelve processes, one payroll cycle

  1. P01Configuration and formulas
  2. P02Pay structure and enrolment
  3. P03Pre-payroll and input
  4. P04Calculation and run management
  5. P05Corrections and retro
  6. P06Obligations and compliance
  7. P07Loans and advances
  8. P08Payslips
  9. P09Payment and disbursement
  10. P10Accounting and GL
  11. P11Period and year-end close
  12. P12Reporting and analytics

Design decisions that shaped it

The engine knows no obligation

Tax bands, pension ceilings and remittance formats are elements, formulas and dated tables. Onboarding a new organisation is configuration, never a code change.

Committed runs are immutable

Once committed, a run is a permanent financial record. Corrections are new records (reversals, supplementaries, arrears) that point back to the original.

Every number is explicable

The calculation trace shows the formula as evaluated, every input and where it came from, proration and rounding, so a non-technical user can explain any figure.

Fail closed

If the engine cannot determine a correct result it stops that employee and raises an exception. Late payroll is recoverable; wrong payroll is not.

CiBS ERP

CiBS Budgeting Module

From budget call to controlled spending

Two connected modules: Budget Preparation, from the budget call to board approval, and Budget Management, which controls spending against what was approved.

Built for
Public and private sector organisations, with revenue, capital, operational and development budgets
My role
Product owner
I authored
Solution designs and PRDs for both modules
Platform
Oracle APEX on Oracle Autonomous Database
Integrates with
General Ledger, Procurement, Payroll and Accounts Payable

The problem

Budgets pass through many hands (department officers, finance, executives, the board) under hard calendar deadlines, especially in government. The product needed ceilings that are enforced, versions that keep their history, and approvals that escalate rather than stall.

What I did

  • Wrote the solution designs and PRDs for both modules: budget cycle initiation, ceilings, proposals, consolidation, multi-level approval and revision on the preparation side; execution, commitment control, fund availability, transfers, reporting and year-end on the management side.
  • Defined role-based responsibilities (initiators, reviewers, approvers and the finance administrator) and the escalation rules for overdue approvals.
Design decisions, process detail and more screenshotsHide the detail

Design decisions that shaped it

Ceilings are enforced at entry

Proposals are checked against departmental ceilings and expected funding before they can move forward.

Every revision is a new version

Rejected or adjusted budgets are saved as new versions, so the full history of a figure is preserved.

Commitment accounting

Obligations are recorded when they are made, such as when a purchase order is raised, not when they are paid, which prevents over-commitment.

Configurable control levels

Organisations choose hard stops or soft warnings with authorised override, and get alerts as utilisation crosses thresholds.

CiBS E-Procurement Suite

CiBS E-Procurement: Planning and Initiation

Every purchase starts with a plan

A full module of the CiBS E-Procurement Suite covering procurement plans and requests, purchase requisitions, approval workflow and budget encumbrance, and generating purchase orders and RFQs from approved requisitions.

Suite
CiBS E-Procurement Suite of Applications
My role
Product owner
Platform
Oracle APEX on Oracle Autonomous Database
I authored
Solution design and PRD
Connects to
CiBS Budgeting Module for fund checks and encumbrance

The problem

Procurement starts long before a purchase order. Organisations need to plan what they will buy, raise requests and requisitions against an approved budget, and stop spending that has not been funded, before any supplier is engaged.

What I did

  • Wrote the solution design and PRD for the Planning and Initiation module: procurement plans, requests, requisitions, approvals and the hand-off to purchase documents.
  • Defined how requisitions reserve budget and how reservations are released, so procurement and budgeting stay in step.
Design decisions, process detail and more screenshotsHide the detail

Design decisions that shaped it

Budget is reserved at requisition

Approved requisitions encumber the budget by cost centre and account, and cancelled ones release it.

One approval console

Plans, requests and requisitions share a single workflow, with order-line detail visible to approvers.

Requisitions become documents

Approved requisition lines can be turned into purchase orders or RFQs manually or automatically, and assigned to a PO officer.

Before product: Oracle E-Business Suite delivery

I started as an Oracle EBS functional consultant across HCM, Payroll and Financials, on government and enterprise implementations. It’s where I learned how enterprise systems succeed or fail inside real organisations.

National Pension Commission (PenCom), Nigeria

Oracle EBS HCM and Payroll re-implementation, one of Counterhouse’s landmark projects. I built and debugged fast formulas for allowances and statutory deductions (house maintenance, rent, meal subsidy, NHF and pension), and delivered documentation and training: training manuals, attendance and feedback analysis, and allowance-eligibility workbooks that cross-reference grades against allowance matrices.

Cross River State Government, Nigeria

Oracle EBS re-implementation for a state government, another of Counterhouse’s landmark projects, spanning HR and payroll.

Government of Lesotho payroll

Oracle EBS Payroll engagement. I produced a pain-points register that separated process-driven issues from product limitations, giving the client and the team a shared, prioritised view of what to fix and how.

Payroll and pension reconciliation

Multi-month PAYE discrepancy investigations across payroll registers and deduction files, and pension reconciliations across several pay periods for a government ministry: finding doubled deductions, correcting them against contribution files and returning reports in the client’s original format.

About me

I work as an Oracle ERP implementation consultant, business analyst and product owner at Counterhouse Consultants, an Oracle implementation and consulting firm working across Africa. I implement Oracle E-Business Suite across HCM, Payroll and Financials for government and enterprise clients, analyse business processes and turn them into clear requirements, and own the SaaS products we build ourselves, from performance management and payroll to budgeting and e-procurement.

Whatever the domain, the job is the same: understand how the business actually works, find where it hurts, and shape technology that fixes it. I’m as comfortable in a workshop with finance, HR or procurement teams as I am with developers debating a data model, and I make sure both conversations end up in the same specification. I work within cross-functional teams of developers, testers, consultants and client staff, and I manage subject matter experts and stakeholders from the first requirements workshop through to sign-off, keeping everyone aligned on what is being built and why. I’m open to Oracle ERP implementation consulting, business analyst and product owner roles.
